title: SDK call-patterns resolver and canonical fixbook
author: Elena Kim
body:
Summary

This playbook explains common SDK call patterns we see in customer and internal integrations, how those patterns interact with the Redwood inference runtime, the important telemetry signals to monitor, and a compact set of canonical fixes for top support issues. The goal is to provide engineers and support to quickly resolve integration issues and optimize for cost/latency without deep runtime knowledge.

Intent and scope

- Audience: SDK authors, integration engineers, Developer Experience (DX) on-call, Customer Support L2/L3.
- Scope: client-side call shapes (single-request, streaming, batched, prefetch/pipeline), retry/idempotency strategies, local cache/encoder patterns, telemetry queries to triage root cause, and step-by-step canonical fixes.
- Not covered: server-side kernel tuning, GPU allocation internals (see eng-serving-runtime docs).

When to use this doc

- You are debugging a customer report that "responses are truncated on streaming" or "cost spiked overnight".
- You are designing an SDK integration and want a validated default for retries, batching windows, and telemetry events.
- You need a short runbook for on-call to triage request-level issues and suggest immediate mitigations.

High-level call patterns and recommended defaults

1) Single-shot generation (synchronous)
- Pattern: client sends prompt -> wait for final completion token -> parse JSON/text output.
- SDK defaults we recommend: timeout=30s, max_tokens=512, retries=1 (idempotent false), content-type=application/json.
- SLO impact: p95 latency depends on model/seq length; aim to keep client timeout >= runtime p95 + 50% cushion.

2) Streaming generation (incremental tokens)
- Pattern: client opens persistent stream, receives chunked tokens/events.
- SDK defaults: heartbeat/ping interval 45s, reconnect backoff jittered 500ms-3s, client-side buffer flush every 120ms.
- Important flags: resume_id (for resuming incomplete streams), allow_partial=true for degraded UX fallback.

3) Bundled/batched requests (multi-prompt or multi-user multiplex)
- Pattern: client aggregates small requests into a single RPC to reduce per-token overhead.
- SDK defaults: bundling window = 15ms (latency-sensitive) or 250ms (throughput-optimized), max batch tokens = 32k, max batch items = 32.
- Observability: track batch_size_histogram and batch_wait_ms. High batch_wait_ms indicates client-side backlog or misconfigured window.

4) Prefetch/encoder-first (embeddings + generation)
- Pattern: compute embeddings or encoded prefixes, stash in cache, then call generation with cached KV.
- SDK defaults: cache_ttl=5m for session-based use; cache eviction by LRU.
- Cost note: redundant embedding calls are a common source of cost spikes — prefer cached embeddings where user flows repeat.

Telemetry signals to collect (client + platform)

Essential events we expect SDKs to emit by default:
- request.start, request.end, request.error (with error_code), stream.ping, stream.resume_attempt, batch.emit_size, auth.token_refresh.

Minimal PromQL examples (Redwood telemetry/Prometheus):
- p95 request latency by model: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="runtime", model=~".*"}[5m])) by (le, model))
- batch wait > 200ms rate: sum(rate(batch_wait_ms_bucket{job="runtime"}[5m])) by (le)
- token cost trend (per hour): increase(token_cost_total[1h])

Trace-level triage checklist (ordered)

1) Reproduce the problem locally with customer inputs (if available) or similar seed prompts.
2) Identify call pattern: single-shot, streaming, batch, prefetch.
3) Pull request-level trace from dx-telemetry or request-id. Typical CLI:

```
redwood dx trace get --id=<request-id> --since=2h
```

4) Inspect the fields: client_sdk_version, user_agent, batch_size, batch_wait_ms, model_variant, kernel_hint, auth_principal.

5) If streaming: check stream.ping and stream.resume_attempt events and server-side stream timeout (default 60s).

Canonical issues, triage notes, and fixes

A) Symptom: Streaming disconnects after ~60s of silence
- Likely cause: intermediary load balancer or client-side idle timeout.
- Evidence: trace shows no stream.ping events, server sent keepalive but client-side closed socket.
- Fix (fast): enable SDK heartbeat/ping at 30–45s and increase server keepalive grace to 90s for affected tenant.
- Fix (permanent): update SDK default to heartbeat=45s and add documentation snippet for proxies (NGINX/Envoy) to set proxy_read_timeout >= 120s.

B) Symptom: Overnight cost spike with many small embedding calls
- Likely cause: embedding calls executed per keystroke or per-character due to unguarded client loop.
- Evidence: token_cost_total and embedding_call_count spiked; many identical inputs; cache miss rate high.
- Fix: add client-side debounce to embedding requests (250–500ms), enable local LRU cache with TTL 5m, and add server-side quota alert rule: rate(embedding_call_count[5m]) > threshold triggers paging to on-call.

C) Symptom: High p50 but normal p95 latency
- Likely cause: batching window too aggressive — some requests wait for window to fill, others go through fast.
- Evidence: batch_wait_ms histogram shows bimodal distribution; batch_size variance high.
- Fix: decrease bundling window for latency-sensitive routes (from 250ms to 20ms) or split critical route to dedicated route with direct non-bundled path.

D) Symptom: Deterministic JSON parse error from model output
- Likely cause: model occasionally emits trailing tokens that break strict JSON parsing.
- Evidence: request response bodies contain JSON + stray characters on retries.
- Fixes: (1) apply tolerant parser on client that strips trailing non-JSON characters; (2) use the model function-calling schema (structured output) when strict structured output required; (3) enable server-side output normalization hook for pinned model versions.

E) Symptom: Frequent 429s after SDK upgrade
- Likely cause: SDK changed retry/backoff or concurrent connection defaults.
- Evidence: spike in client concurrent_connections, rate of retries increased.
- Fix: rollback SDK to previous version or change SDK config: set retries=2, backoff_base=300ms, max_concurrency=10. Communicate recommended config in release notes.

F) Symptom: Duplicate completions (same request returned twice)
- Likely cause: misapplied idempotency key or client-side race where retry occurs after partial success.
- Evidence: two request IDs with identical payload and different timestamps; server logs show first request succeeded but client retried.
- Fix: adopt per-request idempotency_key and server-side dedupe window (60s). Update SDK to surface idempotency_key generation helpers.

Runbook: Immediate mitigations for customer-impacting incidents

1) If customer is blocked (broken UX): temporarily flip to a known-good route/model via the routing API:

```
redwood routes set --tenant=<tenant> --route=/chat --model=gptx-lite-v1 --mode=direct
```

2) If cost runaway: pause non-critical tenants or disable embeddings pipeline for tenant:

```
redwood tenant suspend-ops --id=<tenant> --ops=embeddings
```

3) If latency outlier: enable temporary dedicated burst pool for tenant (5 GPUs) and increase priority:

```
redwood capacity allocate --tenant=<tenant> --pool=burst --gpus=5 --priority=high
```

4) Communicate: post incident-specific status and a minimal repro to #dx-oncall Slack and to the customer within 30 minutes with the mitigation and ETA for a fix.

SDK code examples and recommended config snippets

- Example robust streaming client (pseudo-JS):

```
const client = new RedwoodSDK({heartbeatMs: 45000, resume: true, retries: 2, backoffBaseMs: 500});
const stream = await client.stream.create({model: 'redwood-gen-v1', prompt: userPrompt});
stream.on('token', t => render(t));
stream.on('ping', () => stream.send({type: 'keepalive'}));
stream.on('closed', async meta => { if(meta.resumeable) await client.stream.resume(meta.resume_id); });
```

- Example bundling config (YAML):

```
bundler:
  enabled: true
  window_ms: 20
  max_items: 16
  max_tokens: 16000
```

- Example telemetry event (JSON) for request.start:

```
{
  "event": "request.start",
  "client_sdk_version": "1.8.0",
  "route": "/chat",
  "model": "redwood-gen-v1",
  "user_id": "u-1234",
  "trace_id": "t-abcdef"
}
```

Checklist for SDK authors before release

- Ensure telemetry events above are emitted for all call patterns.
- Confirm default bundling window is documented with guidance for latency vs cost.
- Add examples for proxy keepalives (NGINX/Envoy) in README.
- Run the SDK through the devx-chaos harness (link: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/sdk-chaos-testing-and-resilience-experiments-2026).
- Include migration notes when changing retry/backoff defaults.

Ownership and escalation

- Owner: Developer Experience SDK Team (dx-sdk). Primary on-call: dx-oncall rotation.
- Escalation: dx-oncall -> eng-sre -> runtime-team for kernel/model issues.
- Related pages: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/, /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues/, /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/

Appendix: sample queries and thresholds we use in alerts

- Alert: streaming.disconnect_rate > 0.02 for 10m -> page dx-oncall
- Alert: embed_call_rate_per_tenant > 1000/min -> create high-priority ticket and throttle tenant
- Alert: p95_latency(model="redwood-gen-v1") > 800ms for 5m -> page eng-sre

Table: quick reference fixes

| Symptom | Immediate mitigation | Long-term fix | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Streaming disconnects | increase client heartbeat to 30s | update SDK defaults & proxy docs | dx-sdk |
| Cost spike embeddings | debounce client + enable cache | TTL-based cache + quota | dx-sdk + billing |
| High batch wait | reduce bundling window for route | route split to dedicated low-latency pool | dx-sdk + runtime |
| JSON parse errors | tolerant parser | function-calling schema | dx-sdk + model-onboarding |

Notes and history

- 2026-10-15: initial draft by Elena Kim.
- 2026-12-11: added embedding cost mitigation and debounce recommendation after two customer incidents.
- 2027-02-20: promoted to published after reviewer approvals and added CLI mitigation commands.

If you have additional canonical fixes to add, file a PR to this page and ping dx-sdk for review.
